candidates.hypothesis: Adding interaction features or higher-order combinations via `features.py` will improve representational capacity.
candidates.information_value: Tests whether feature interaction preprocessing improves sparse categorical embedding spaces on small interaction datasets.
candidates.mechanism: By enriching the categorical representation with combinations of fields, the Factorization Machine can capture non-linear feature interactions that are absent in single-field lookups.

candidates.hypothesis: Switching from pointwise BCE loss to pairwise BPR / margin ranking loss via config.json and train.py will better optimize ranking metrics (GAUC, nDCG@5).
candidates.information_value: Determines if ranking-oriented loss objectives outperform pointwise classification on this account-grouped metric.
candidates.mechanism: Pointwise loss optimizes absolute click probability rather than relative order within an account, whereas pairwise optimization directly aligns with the ranking task.
candidates.novelty_vs_history: Config already mentions pairwise loss mode support in train.py, but champion uses pointwise.

candidates.hypothesis: Increasing `neg_per_pos` and batch size in training will stabilize gradient updates and improve generalization.
candidates.information_value: Quantifies the sensitivity of the model to mini-batch noise and negative sampling ratio.
candidates.mechanism: Larger batch sizes and balanced negative sampling reduce variance in stochastic gradient updates, mitigating the high train-dev gap.

candidates.hypothesis: Increasing weight decay (`l2`) and dropout or learning rate scheduling will reduce the train-dev gap.
candidates.information_value: Measures the impact of regularization strength on generalizability given the large train-dev gap.
candidates.mechanism: Stronger L2 regularization penalizes large embedding norms, preventing the model from memorizing sparse user-product interactions.

candidates.hypothesis: Adding a small MLP projection or bias term modifications in `model.py` will enhance expressive power beyond pure second-order factorization.
candidates.information_value: Tests whether deep architectures outperform traditional Factorization Machines on this dataset.
candidates.mechanism: Pure FM captures linear and pairwise interactions; adding higher-order or non-linear dense layers on top can capture complex feature interactions.

candidates.hypothesis: Applying temperature scaling or rank calibration post-processing on predicted scores will align probabilities and improve ranking metrics.
candidates.information_value: Determines if post-hoc score calibration provides measurable gains on ranking metrics.
candidates.mechanism: Calibrating score distributions per account group ensures scores reflect proper relative ordering probabilities.
